reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 only mentions cold spraying of a different HEA (CrMnFeCoNi) on a different substrate (aluminium alloy) without reporting coating quality, while E2 shows that the specific CoCrFeNiMo0.85 composition is prone to manufacturing cracking when deposited via laser metal deposition, directly contradicting the premise of reduced cracking. No evidence is provided for the claimed benefits of cold spray for this alloy or the effect of pre-treatment.
premises: Cold spray can deposit a dense, fine-grained, metallurgically bonded CoCrFeNiMo0.85 HEA coating on 316L stainless steel.
Cold spray avoids melting, thereby preventing hot cracking associated with fusion welding.
The CoCrFeNiMo0.85 HEA composition improves hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance.
Pre-surface roughening and optimized parameters ensure robust interfacial adhesion.
